Intentional: pack request bodies now require numeric osquery version strings (e.g. "5.19.0", "5.12", "5") for min_osquery_version and for per-query queries.<id>.version ("" still inherits the pack's min_osquery_version, or no constraint if the pack has none). Non-numeric values such as "latest" or "5.x" were previously accepted and stored but never ran on a 5.x agent: osqueryd's versionAtLeast check fails for them, so the query was silently dropped from the schedule (osquerybeat's RRULE scheduler likewise skips versions it cannot parse). A few other now-rejected shapes (e.g. "5.10.0.1", "5.10.0-rc1", whitespace-padded values) did run, because versionAtLeast returns at the first differing part and trims each part. min_osquery_version was added on main in 2026-09 and has not shipped in a stateful release. Responses are unchanged: stored legacy values are still returned as-is.

Intentional: per-query queries.<id>.version in pack request bodies is capped at 64 characters, matching the existing min_osquery_version cap. Valid values are numeric osquery versions (e.g. "5.19.0"), so no working value is affected.

Intentional: query parameters gain maximum lengths. kuery and userIds accept 65,536 characters, more than the longest URL Kibana accepts (Node's default 65,535-octet HTTP/2 header list; 16 KiB over HTTP/1), so no request that reaches the route today is rejected. nextPage (4,096) is a server-generated cursor of a few hundred characters, sourceFilters (64) fits every combination of its three allowed values, and startDate/endDate (64) fit ISO timestamps and date math.
